name: Amiodarone
route_note: oral loading then maintenance tablets; IV infusion for acute arrhythmias and cardiac arrest

discovery.note: Developed from khellin as an antianginal; its antiarrhythmic action was recognised later, notably by Bramah Singh.

tagline: Highly effective, iodine-rich antiarrhythmic with a months-long half-life
summary: Amiodarone is an iodinated benzofuran antiarrhythmic that blocks potassium, sodium and calcium channels and beta-adrenoceptors. It is among the most effective drugs for ventricular and atrial arrhythmias but is limited by thyroid, lung, liver, eye and skin toxicity.
mechanism: Amiodarone's main effect is blockade of the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr, hERG/KCNH2), prolonging the action potential and refractory period in all cardiac tissues (class III).

It also blocks inactivated sodium channels (class I), L-type calcium channels (class IV) and has non-competitive anti-adrenergic effects (class II). This mix causes QT prolongation but relatively little torsades de pointes.
It contains about 37% iodine by weight and inhibits peripheral conversion of T4 to T3, explaining both hypo- and hyperthyroidism.
uses: Life-threatening recurrent ventricular fibrillation or haemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia
Shock-refractory VF/pulseless VT in cardiac arrest (IV)
Off-label: maintenance of sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Developed at Labaz in Belgium as an antianginal drug.

history.title: Antiarrhythmic action
history.detail: Bramah Singh and Vaughan Williams describe its class III antiarrhythmic properties.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Cordarone tablets for life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.

history.title: ARREST
history.detail: IV amiodarone improves survival to hospital admission in shock-refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

history.title: SCD-HeFT
history.detail: Amiodarone does not reduce mortality in heart failure, whereas an ICD does.

history.title: Nexterone
history.detail: A premixed IV formulation without polysorbate 80 is approved.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 to active desethylamiodarone; inhibits CYP3A4, 2C9, 2D6 and P-gp

safety.boxed_warning: For life-threatening arrhythmias only because of substantial toxicity: pulmonary toxicity (can be fatal), hepatic injury and worsened arrhythmia; initiate in hospital.

facts: Its large volume of distribution (around 60 L/kg) and fat storage explain the very long half-life.
It markedly increases warfarin and digoxin levels.

references.title: Kudenchuk PJ et al. Amiodarone for resuscitation after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation (ARREST). N Engl J Med 1999
